notes: Title: 'Epidermal Growth Factor-stimulated Human Cervical Cancer Cell Growth is Associated with EGFR and Cyclin D1 Activation, Independent of COX-2 Expression Levels.' claim_type_screen_label was clinical_observational -- a false positive; this is a preclinical cell-line mechanism study, not a clinical claim, and does not belong in the candidate pool at all. Caught on sight during batch 1 work-queue preparation, before any research time was spent on it. Consistent with the screen's known ~85% precision (ADR-021) -- expected occasional false positives, human review catches them for free at this stage, exactly as designed.

Title: "Fractalkine Attenuates Microglial Cell Activation Induced by Prenatal Stress." claim_type_screen_label was clinical_observational -- a false positive; this is an in-vitro microglial cell-culture study, not a clinical claim about patients, treatment, or clinical outcomes. Caught during batch 3 raw-material preparation (item 13). This is the SECOND candidate rejected for this exact failure mode -- the first was rw-5833 (2026-08-06, EGFR/cervical cancer cell-line study). Two false positives of this kind out of 17 total work-queue draws so far (~12%) is within the screen's known ~84% precision (ADR-021, ~16% expected imprecision) -- not yet evidence the screen's recall tuning has gone too far, but worth continuing to track if a third instance appears.

Title: "Six different hemofiltration devices for blood conservation in cardiac surgery." Boldt J, Zickmann B, Fedderson B, Herold C, Dapper F, Hempelmann G. Ann Thorac Surg 1991;51(5):747-753. PMID 2025077. The original 1991 abstract has been overwritten in PubMed's own structured record: its <Abstract> field now contains only the retraction statement, not the original text -- confirmed directly against PubMed's own EFetch XML, not merely hard to find elsewhere. No trap claim can be written without fabricating the content it would need to represent. Retraction notice (PMID 28219541) is itself specific and well-verified (names the exact mechanism: results altered relative to co-author Berend Fedderson's own doctoral thesis on the same study) -- it is the SOURCE material that is unrecoverable, not the notice. This is a distinct failure mode from notice_specificity=unverifiable/bare (which concern the notice) and from no_institutional_source (which concerns current evidence) -- here the retracted paper's own original content is gone from the record that would normally preserve it.

Title: "Adjunctive Electroconvulsive Therapy for Schizophrenia: A Meta-analysis of Randomized Rater-Masked Controlled Trials." Rejected for AUTHOR-GROUP CONCENTRATION (ADR-031 amendment), a third, distinct rejection reason from eligibility failure (e.g. rw-18340) and topical redundancy (e.g. rw-6531). Shares 8 of 11 authors (Wei Zheng, Yu-Tao Xiang, Ying-Qiang Xiang, Xiao-Lan Cao, Tong Guo, Zheng-Rong Liu, Helen F K Chiu, Gabor S Ungvari) with rw-5690 (item 14, kept) -- 72.7% overlap of the smaller author list, the same core research team publishing two closely related ECT-for-schizophrenia meta-analyses in 2016, both retracted. Individually this would sit exactly at ADR-031s original per-author cap of 2, not exceed it, but the author sharing is so extensive the two papers are effectively one research unit -- the amended rule (ADR-031 follow-up) treats papers sharing a majority of authors as a single unit for cap purposes. Item 14 kept instead: its gold claim direction is contradictory (current evidence reverses the trap claim), the rarer and harder shape, against item 11s concordant (narrowing) direction.

Title: "Efficacy of risedronate against hip fracture in patients with neurological diseases: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials." Rejected for REDUNDANCY, distinct from both eligibility failure (e.g. rw-18340) and author-group concentration (e.g. rw-5667) -- a third and fourth distinct rejection reason, now four total. Near-duplicate of item 7 (record 6414, kept): same author cluster (Iwamoto/Matsumoto/Takeda), same drug class (bisphosphonate fracture prevention), same population shape (elderly patients with a neurological comorbidity), and the same no-current-answer structure. Two near-identical items would add repetition to the benchmark, not coverage -- rejected on that basis, not because the candidate itself is ineligible.

Title: "Evaluation of Impact of Pregnancy on Oral Health Status and Oral Health Related Quality of Life among Women of Kashmir Valley." No institutional source (systematic review/guideline/regulatory statement) found for this specific epidemiological claim (pregnancy effect on periodontal/oral health status). More importantly, a genuine circular-provenance risk was found and is the primary reason for rejection rather than mere absence of evidence: the only Kashmir-valley OHIP-14 figures located during eligibility search may themselves be citing this retracted paper's own data, not an independent source -- this was flagged but not resolved when item 16's raw material was first prepared (results/item16_raw_material.md). Rejecting rather than risk importing the retracted claim into a gold claim through an uncorrected downstream citation -- the exact failure this benchmark measures, occurring inside our own annotation process. Logged as a real, encountered hazard (ADR-058's independence-verification rule exists for exactly this), not a hypothetical -- belongs in the paper's methods as such.
